notes: Heron is Adetunji Dahunsi's Compose Multiplatform Bluesky client (Android, desktop, iOS). No "modules": the previews are spread one or two per module across about twenty-five modules — one route-level screen preview in nearly every :feature:* module, plus the MorphingLoader and Halo previews in :ui:core and the inference sheet in :ui:sheets — so picking one would publish a single screen; this renders them all, as horologist does. renderer: desktop, and upstream has already prepared for exactly that: every module gets jvm("desktop") from its kotlin-multiplatform convention, and ui-module-convention adds compose.desktop.currentOs to desktopMain as runtimeOnly with the comment "Host skiko native for the compose-preview Desktop renderer (the CLI injects the plugin, not skiko)". The previews live in commonMain and import androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview.Preview, the multiplatform alias, so they compile into the desktop target. The Android side uses com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library (AGP 9.3), which is a further reason not to take the Robolectric lane first. The feature previews render whole routes through upstream's own RoutePreview harness with no-op state mutators and stub timeline state holders, and most of them start from the route's empty State.Immutable(), so expect several near-empty screens; only home, inference, profile, post-detail, conversation and gallery seed real content. Nothing in them is meant to reach DI or the network, but whole-route previews are how imports of this shape fail, so that is the thing to watch on the first render. previewAnnotations names the two multipreviews the source pre-flight cannot see through: MessageListPreviews (:feature:messages, two widths) and FontScalePreviews (:feature:conversation, three font scales). Two previews are left out of the inventory but not excluded: :composeApp's App() is the KMP template's leftover "Click me!" greeting and :androidApp's AppAndroidPreview just wraps it; MessageListFixedHeightPreview is upstream's reproduction of a since-fixed clipping bug and is kept beside its fix rather than captioned.
